content:
Maria: Heads-up — last night we saw ~140 ECC/Xid spikes across 6 nodes between 02:10–02:40 UTC. Many looked like single-sample blips that immediately recovered. This noisy churn triggered automation and started node drains. Looking for safe tuning approaches to reduce false positives without masking real flakies.

Raj: I saw the same. A lot were 1-sample spikes, then zeroes. Our current rule is too eager and the downstream automation treats any alert as a candidate for immediate drain.

Ollie: What does the current Prom rule look like? We scrape dcgm exporter and have a per-card counter, right? Could we move to increase() over a longer window or require sustained rate?

Maria: Simplified current rule we have now (pseudo):

```
- alert: GPU_ECC_XID_HIGH
  expr: increase(nvidia_dcgm_ecc_xid_total[5m]) > 0.1
  for: 0m
  labels:
    severity: critical
```

This fires on tiny blips. Proposal: aggregate by card, require sustained increases across multiple windows (hysteresis), and add a short suppression for cards that rapidly recover. Also demote first alert to warning.

Sam: Sketch of a more conservative rule — use increase over 10m, group_by card id, and a `for: 10m` to avoid transient fires. Example:

```
- alert: GPU_ECC_XID_SUSTAINED
  expr: increase(nvidia_dcgm_ecc_xid_total[10m]) > 1
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Sustained ECC/Xid errors on {{ $labels.card }}"
```

Raj: LGTM. Also consider `resets()` or rate() semantics if counter resets are noisy. We can add `unless` clauses to ignore nodes that had driver rollouts in the past 30m (they tend to spike).

dcgm-bot: dcgm_exporter: scrape on node=ml-12 gpu=card-2 failed at 2025-11-03T02:20:13Z (transient, recovered).

Maria: Important: change alertmanager routes so initial alerts are grouped/aggregated and don't immediately page SRE. We should: 1) set first-severity to warning, 2) only escalate to pager after 30m or 3 repeated firings, and 3) group by card_serial and node to dedupe duplicates.

Ollie: Also add a Prometheus recording rule to compute `card_ecc_rate = increase(...[15m])` so dashboards and runbooks can use the smoothed value. That makes posthoc triage easier.

Raj: Operational tweak: stop auto-drain on first alert. Modify the drain playbook to require either manual ack or two consecutive alerts with at least 5m between them. We can mark a card as "needs-replacement" after X repeats instead of immediate node drain.

Sam: I'll open a PR with: the tuned Prom rules, a recording rule for smoothed ECC/Xid rate, Alertmanager route changes (group_by card_serial/node + inhibit/continue), and an update to the drain runbook. Want me to include rollback steps and a metric to track false_positive rate?

Maria: Yes please include a false_positive metric (alerts that resolved within <10m) and a short experiment plan: run tuned rules in warning mode for 7 days, measure page volume and false positives, then flip severity/escalation if stable. :thumbsup:

alert-manager: Note — existing route `gpu-critical` will need a small change, will open a config PR in infra/monitoring.

Sam: Added to my TODOs, aiming to get a PR up today. I'll tag @Maria and @Raj for review and include the exact config snippets and backout.

Maria: Thanks — this should reduce noisy ops and lower unnecessary drains while still catching real card flakiness. We'll reconvene after 7 days of data.
